value.title: dd — build wishlist
value.note: Candidate work, NOT a plan. Nothing here is scheduled, allocated or attested — a row graduates by becoming a builder plan, at which point it flips to `planned` and the plan owns it. Opened 2026-08-08 on Jordan's ask, immediately after his OQ-1 ruling that dd ships a supported LIBRARY surface and not merely a CLI. Kept as a dd document rather than prose so the rows are queryable and the render is deterministic.

value.title: SDK design flow — research best-in-class SDK design guidelines, then design dd's public surface against them
value.why: Jordan's OQ-1 ruling (2026-08-08) makes dd an SDK, not a CLI with an accidental import surface. The current exports map was derived from what harness happened to import (dossier F-04), which is a description of one consumer rather than a designed API. An SDK that ships under semver needs a surface chosen on purpose.
value.blocked_on: plan 001 closing out first — Jordan: 'close out current work then creaet a new builder flow on the SDK'
value.source: Jordan 2026-08-08, verbatim in plan 001 open_questions OQ-1 note
value.note: Jordan specified the research step explicitly: best-in-class SDK design guidelines via perplexity, BEFORE designing. Its own builder flow, not an extension of plan 001. Inputs already measured and waiting for it: the runtime exports probe (scripts/exports-reachability-probe.mjs), koala's consumer census (4 surviving files, 4 live symbols), and the root-export defect below. ACCEPTANCE TEST, set by Jordan's OQ-2 ruling 2026-08-08 and measurable rather than a taste question: HARNESS RE-IMPLEMENTS `plan validate` USING PUBLIC EXPORTS ONLY. Today's answer is NO, by exactly five symbols (DEFAULT_GATE_TERMINAL_STATES, deriveItems, effectiveRel, collectDeclaredRels, isRecord — lg-000b). Design the surface around the PLAN USE CASE as the driving case: it is the hardest known consumer, exercising typed links, cardinality, cross-document traversal, derived state and gate semantics simultaneously, so a surface that expresses it expresses almost anything simpler. Jordan: "SDK shoudl be super rich."

value.title: Fix Windows drive-letter re-anchoring at three sites
value.why: LIVE PRODUCT DEFECT in the shipped CLI. `startsWith('/')` misreads a drive-letter path as relative, so `C:/Users/x` becomes `<repoRoot>/C:/Users/x`. Two of the three sites back `dd doctor --path` and `dd graph --path`, so it reaches users directly.
value.blocked_on: Jordan's call: hotfix now vs plan 002
value.source: backlog #22 — found by pij-related-koala reading this fork, reproduced here before recording
value.note: core/validate.ts:88 is the one that matters most: byte-identical to upstream, and upstream deliberately deferred its fix to a later PR, so it will NEVER arrive by forward port. Not a separator bug — toPosix does not fix it. Two distinct families per upstream's own split; do not port as one change.

value.title: Add `prepare` so a git-URL install produces a working package
value.why: `npm install github:AI-Substrate/dd` reports SUCCESS and installs a broken package — no dist/, bin throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. We have `prepack` but npm runs `prepare` on git installs, and dist/ is gitignored. A failure that looks like success.
value.blocked_on: Jordan's call on whether to land it now or behind the distribution decision
value.source: measured 2026-08-08 while answering Jordan's git-URL distribution question
value.note: One line. Fix verified against a real git install: dist/ builds, bin runs, envelope correct. Live defect regardless of which distribution method is chosen.

value.title: Decide and implement the distribution method: git-URL dependency vs npm publish
value.why: Jordan raised distributing to harness via the git repo rather than npm. A git DEPENDENCY serves both the bin and library imports; `npx`-the-runner serves only the CLI and gives harness nothing importable, which does not fit the four surviving library consumers.
value.note: Measured: the exports map gates IDENTICALLY under a git install — ./plan is still ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED — so the distribution method does NOT answer OQ-2. It does soften the freeze: without publishing, freezing stops being a semver promise to strangers and becomes 'do not break harness'. Choosing git-URL would let the whole release apparatus stay permanently inert.

value.title: Fix the root export so importing the package does not execute the CLI
value.why: `.` resolves to dist/index.js, which IS the bin entry — it carries the node shebang and calls main(). So `import '@ai-substrate/dd'` runs the CLI, prints help to stdout, and yields zero named exports. Harmless to harness today (it imports subpaths only) but wrong for an SDK.
value.blocked_on: nothing technically — but it must land BEFORE any exports freeze, since a freeze is when a latent defect becomes permanent
value.source: surfaced by the runtime exports probe, predicted by koala from the same defect in harness-engineering
value.note: Already inside tk-0002's scope for exactly the freeze-timing reason. Listed here too because it is a real SDK-surface defect in its own right and wl-0001 will care about it.

value.title: Mechanize the two guardrails that are still pure discipline
value.why: Plan 001 shipped guardrails against claims outrunning evidence, but only some are enforced. The out-of-diff assertion sweep and measured-at stamping are still human discipline — nothing fails if a reviewer skips the sweep or a receipt omits its SHA. A rule not yet mechanized is a rule we pay for in attention every review.
value.source: SUGG-001, raised by the PM and endorsed 2026-08-07; sits in the migrated backlog
value.note: Two candidate instruments: a gate over assertions naming changed behaviour outside the diff, and a linter that every count-claim in an execution log carries a resolvable SHA. Precedent exists — `just check-orient` and `just check-handover` both started as discipline and became gates.

value.title: Calculated columns and rows — derived tallies, recomputed on edit
value.why: A total typed into a table is a claim that goes stale the moment any row it summarises changes, and nothing detects it — precisely the class plan 001 spent four phases cataloguing: a figure that was true when written. dd already renders .dd.md deterministically from .dd.json, so a tally computed at build time CANNOT rot: it is derived, never asserted, and `dd build --check` already fails on drift. This turns a whole category of stale-number defect into an impossibility rather than a discipline.
value.blocked_on: shape not settled — see the open questions in the note
value.source: Jordan 2026-08-08, verbatim: "next wishlist item is calculated columns (auto gens the total on edits, ato adds total column at bottom. cal tally cols and rows with setting."
value.note: AS ASKED: totals regenerate on edit (any set/add/rm touching a tallied section), a total row is appended automatically, and both column and row tallies are configurable by a setting. OPEN SHAPE QUESTIONS, recorded rather than guessed: (1) does the setting live in the SCHEMA — a field declares itself summable, so every document of that type tallies alike — or in the DOCUMENT, per-instance? Schema-side is more deterministic and matches how dd resolves everything else; document-side is more flexible. (2) Which aggregates: sum only, or count/min/max/mean? (3) Do tallies MATERIALISE into the .dd.json, or exist only in the rendered .dd.md? Render-only keeps the source a single truth and avoids write amplification on every edit, which argues strongly for it — and it is the option that makes the total underivable-from-anything-but-the-data. (4) What happens to a non-numeric or empty cell in a tallied column — skip, zero, or refuse? Refusing fits this repo: a silently-skipped cell produces a wrong total that looks right, which is the exact failure mode the feature exists to remove.

value.title: Custom validation — semantic rules as portable, declarable data rather than dd code
value.why: Today dd validates STRUCTURE (does this field match the schema shape) while the SEMANTIC rules — a plan must have acceptance criteria, an AC must link to a task, a task's state derives from its assertions — live as hard-coded TypeScript in services/dd/plan. That means only we can express a semantic rule, only for the document families we shipped, and every new discipline needs a code change and a release. Making the rules declarable turns dd from 'a validator that knows about builder plans' into 'a validator anyone can teach', and lets a team encode its own conventions without forking us.
value.blocked_on: wl-0001 — this is an SDK-surface decision and should be designed inside that flow, not ahead of it
value.source: Jordan 2026-08-08, verbatim: "i want the rules that we usein pln to be expressable via a portable and customisable validation concept somehow so anyone can implement semantic validation across the top (plans must have acs, acs mst link to tasks in this file) etc. This will rely heavily on the typing system (ac must have at least one link to typeof tasks.dd/tasklist or what ever)." Raised in the same breath as his note on OQ-2 — "ah yes, but later we will remove" — which is the strategic point below.
value.note: THIS IS THE THING THAT MAKES services/dd/plan REMOVABLE, which is why Jordan raised it while answering OQ-2. Whatever we decide about shipping plan/ publicly is a TRANSITIONAL answer: once semantic rules are declarable, the hard-coded plan semantics become a set of rules attached to the builder/plan schema, and the module carrying them stops needing to exist as a public export. Decide OQ-2 for today's consumer, not for all time. IT LEANS ON THE TYPE SYSTEM, which dd already has and which is the real asset here: links are already rel-typed and target-typed (a proven_by must point at builder/execution-log/section/entries, and E406 link-type-mismatch already fires when it does not). Jordan's example — an AC must carry at least one link of type X to a document of type Y — is a CARDINALITY constraint over an existing typed edge, not a new concept. That is a strong sign the rule vocabulary can be small. SHAPE QUESTIONS for the design flow, recorded not guessed: (1) where do rules live — beside the schema (travelling with the family, so any repo resolving that schema inherits its rules) or in the consuming repo (local conventions over a shared family)? Both are wanted; the resolution order matters more than either. (2) How expressive: declarative predicates over the typed graph (cardinality, required-link-of-type, cross-document reachability) or an escape hatch to real code? A jiti-loaded custom type already exists as precedent for the escape hatch. (3) Are violations errors, warnings, or severity-declared by the rule? The plan validator already distinguishes ERROR from contradiction-class WARN, so severity is already a live concept. (4) NON-VACUITY: a rule engine can silently match nothing. Every rule needs to be provably capable of firing — the same requirement this repo puts on its own guards, and the reason plan 001 found a pin whose docstring claimed more than it pinned.
